verdict.rationale: Twilio Video is API-first. Its documented REST API manages Rooms (name, type, TURN configuration, callbacks, participant limits), Recordings and Compositions, and native SDKs cover client functionality, so much of the product is clearly programmable. However, no evidence states or shows that everything available in the Twilio Console or UI is also exposed through the API, so parity is implied rather than proven. Missing for 10: an explicit API/UI parity statement, evidence that console-level settings and management (e.g. Video Insights, account configuration) are API-accessible, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Use this API to set Room properties such as its name, type, TURN configuration, webhook status callback URL, and the maximum number of Participants.
Status Callbacks allow you to receive events related to the REST resources managed by Twilio: Rooms, Recordings, and Compositions.
Configure a `StatusCallback` URL when creating a Room using the REST API
Twilio Video offers native SDKs for JavaScript (Web), iOS (Swift/Objective-C), and Android (Java/Kotlin).
